title: 20-minute full-body strength
equipment: Dumbbells; chair and clear floor space. Home swaps use a wall or counter and a resistance band.
plan:
From Kelsey Holden’s “Strength training when you only have 20 minutes”:
https://holden.health/20-minute-strength-workout.html

THE 20-MINUTE PLAN
Minutes 0–3: Warm up. March briskly, do 8 chair squats, 8 wall push-ups, and 8 slow hip hinges. Repeat if time allows.
Minutes 3–18: Strength circuit. Complete 8–12 controlled reps of each move below. Rest when you need it. Repeat for 2–3 rounds.
Minutes 18–20: Finish and reset. Walk slowly, breathe, and note what weight or variation you used.

MOVEMENTS AND HOME SWAPS
Goblet squat — sit-to-stand from a chair.
Dumbbell chest press — wall or counter push-up.
Dumbbell Romanian deadlift — bodyweight hip hinge.
One-arm dumbbell row — band row.
Suitcase carry, 30 seconds per side — dead bug, 6–10 reps per side.

HOW HARD SHOULD IT FEEL?
Choose a version that lets you move with control and could leave roughly two or three good repetitions in reserve at the end of a set. The last few reps should feel challenging, but your form should not unravel. You do not need to train to failure for a short workout to count.

New to an exercise? Start with the home swap or a light load. Pain is not a sign of an effective workout. Stop if you feel sharp, sudden, or worsening pain, dizziness, chest pain, or unusual shortness of breath, and seek appropriate medical guidance.

HOW TO MAKE IT WORK OVER TIME
Repeat this workout twice per week on nonconsecutive days. When you can complete the top of the rep range with steady form, make one small change: add a little weight, add one or two reps, slow the lowering phase, or use a slightly harder variation. Change one thing at a time.

If 20 minutes disappears, do one round. The habit still gets a vote.

General education for healthy adults. Get medical clearance when appropriate and see https://holden.health/disclaimer.html.

APP GUIDE
The player walks through two rounds, offers an optional third round, then a reset. The elapsed-time clock does not advance movements automatically. Move at your pace and use Next movement when ready.
